name: Zika virus
short_description: Enveloped flavivirus (genus Orthoflavivirus, ~40-65 nm, roughly 50 nm) with a +ssRNA genome (~10.7 kb) wrapped by a relatively unstructured capsid (C) protein shell, surrounded by a host-derived lipid envelope. The defining feature is the outer surface: 180 copies of the envelope (E) glycoprotein sit as 90 head-to-tail dimers lying FLAT against the membrane in an icosahedral herringbone raft, giving a smooth, tiled, spike-free surface. Spread by day-biting Aedes mosquitoes; usually mild or unnoticed, but crosses the placenta and can disturb fetal brain development.

textbook.2: PASS - re-prompted to explicitly forbid a bowl/plate/container and instead describe concentric rings like a cut orange: a believable 3D sphere with a wedge sliced away showing nested concentric shells (gold tangled +ssRNA genome at centre, pale capsid ring, thin grey-lilac envelope ring) touching directly with no gap or vessel, and the entire uncut outer two-thirds of the sphere smoothly tiled edge-to-edge with flat interlocking herringbone chevron panels - textured but perfectly smooth in silhouette, no spikes/studs/bumps anywhere. Muted educational palette, thin clean outlines, no text/border/vignette, fills the frame on a dark charcoal background. Chosen as label base.

sem.1: PASS - photorealistic false-colour SEM of a single small, perfectly round virion: cool blue-lilac surface entirely tiled edge-to-edge in a neat herringbone/basket-weave texture (facets and seams only), silhouette stays a clean continuous sphere with absolutely nothing projecting - no spikes, no studs, no rays. Surface only (correct for SEM - no interior shown), dark uncluttered background, no baked text/scale bar/border. This is the cleanest 'smooth spike-free surface' read of all four styles. Accepted on the first attempt.

3d.1: PASS - natural biological tints, three layers correctly ordered and distinct: warm gold tangled +ssRNA genome at the centre, a pale warm grey-tan capsid band directly around it, a cool grey-lilac lipid envelope band outside that, and the entire uncut outer surface smoothly tiled edge-to-edge with flat interlocking herringbone panels (golf-ball/rattan-weave texture, silhouette stays perfectly smooth and round, nothing projects). Soft studio lighting, dark seamless background, no neon/monochrome, no text/border. Accepted without needing a second attempt.

watercolor.1: PASS - warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge-to-edge with a soft darker wash halo directly on the paper (no mat/sheet-on-surface, matching cocci/rod-bacterium house style); a vesica-shaped cutaway shows a coppery-gold coiled genome squiggle at the centre, a tan/orange capsid band, and a pale cream envelope band, all touching directly; the uncut top/bottom caps of the sphere are painted with the same flat interlocking herringbone tiling as the other styles, silhouette one smooth continuous hand-drawn curve with nothing poking out. Fine ink outlines, no baked text, no border/frame. Accepted on the first attempt.

reference: PASS (group reference, resolution-limited) - CDC PHIL ID 20538, public-domain digitally colorized TEM (Cynthia Goldsmith, 2016) showing ~15 round, false-colour-red Zika virions scattered through false-colour-purple brain tissue. Directly verified by visual inspection: no baked-in text, arrow or scale bar (unlike the companion greyscale plate PHIL 20487, which has a baked-in arrow and was rejected for that reason). This is a group shot rather than a single isolated particle - honestly the best public-domain resolution available for a ~40-50 nm flavivirus at conventional TEM magnification; individual particle shape, size and count are clearly readable, but the herringbone surface texture is below this plate's resolution. fetch_reference.py used the native 700x700 px source directly and upscaled (Lanczos) to the standard 1080x1080 canvas - noted explicitly as an upscale, not additional real detail.
